column1: # What the probe's TLS strictness actually cost the registry — measured, 2026-10-20.
# tools/jo_tls.py was added because ssl.create_default_context() refuses
# handshakes the ENGINE completes: yamaguchi-opendata.jp answers
# TLSV1_ALERT_INSUFFICIENT_SECURITY to Python's default and HTTP 200 at
# DEFAULT@SECLEVEL=1 with verification still on, while the engine stores 102
# records from it across 3 requests. That recovered 20 of the 27 rows the
# page-2 sweep had written down as dead endpoints.
# The obvious next question is how many CANDIDATES the same strictness had
# refused over the tree's history — a probe that rejects a live source is the
# failure direction that costs sources permanently, because a rejected row
# never ships. Eight batch-reject files name a TLS refusal, 51 distinct
# candidates between them. Every one was re-asked with the new context:
#   STILL_FAILS 30  CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED (an untrusted chain, which a
#                   cipher security level does not address and which must not
#                   be bypassed) or TLSV1_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME (an SNI mismatch)
# AND THE COST WAS ZERO, which is only sayable because it was measured rather
# * 20 of the 21 alive are `jp-kkj-*` — the SAME kkj.go.jp procurement corpus
#   this session rebuilt as 47 prefecture rows reading it exhaustively over a
#   date-window cycle, plus two entity pivots. They were rejected once for a
#   TLS artefact, re-registered by hand later, and are now read in full. Adding
# * the 1 remaining, JO41_WP_CORP_7991 (www.mamiya-op.co.jp), serves five posts
#   titled "Sample post5" dated 2022-07-12 — a demo WordPress install's default
#   content, not corporate notices. It stays out, and that is a judgement about
#   the CONTENT rather than about the transport.
# * the 30 that still fail, fail for the engine too. Measured on four of them:
#   IODA (x3), Dataverse UCLA, NADA Nepal and NI MARENA all answer `rc=-1` and
#   file a collector-fetch-failure record naming it.
# So the tool defect was real and worth fixing — it was actively mislabelling
# 20 live registered rows as dead — and it had cost the registry nothing.
